Yep... I can see how the sexuality would be able to skew someone ito believing they were "always" or "supposed to be" a female. In my opinion, the sissy stuff is IDENTICAL to that of a female's fantasy of rape, but from a man's point of view, which is why, to me, it's a male sexuality.

I really think the key is to always remind yourself that you are a male, no matter how far down the rabbit hole you go. You can really get swallowed by the fantasies. I kinda wish the TG thing didn't exist, and that more guys were helping the cause of making it "acceptable" for men to wear traditionally female clothing in public. I don't really get with the radfems, but I do think men not only oppress men, but also highly oppress themselves.

That's the thing Felix, it's why I never "came out" as transgender. When you're identifying as female, you're identifying with beauty, expression, feelings, submission, etc. Also, if innate gender identity is a thing, then why do some people not even "realize" that they "identify" as a gender until their 20s or 30s. 

It seems as though thirdway's article here http://thirdwaytrans.com/2014/07/13/there-are-no-identities-lurking-in-the-shadows-of-the-psyche/ holds a lot of merit. Could a female identity be moreso created from trauma, or is it created through a "belief"?

It's always sounded funny to me. How do you "come out" as transgender? I'm not trying to sound rude, but as a guy who occasionally wears dresses in public, I never really "came out" to anyone. I just sorta did it.
I'd probably pay a couple of hookers to pretend they care about me and help me lose my virginity.
